pkg_07_os_deadlocks.topic: Deadlock Characterization, Prevention, and Banker's Algorithm

children.name: Four Coffman Conditions (Mutual Exclusion, Hold & Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait)
Deadlock Prevention via Ascending Resource Ordering F(R)
Available, Max, Allocation, and Need Matrices
Numerical 3-Process Safety Test Revealing Unsafe State

episodes.dominant_concept: Deadlock definition & resource competition
The four Coffman conditions
Prevention vs Avoidance & Safe State concept
Banker data structures & Need calculation
Numerical trace discovering unsafe state
Scope notice: omission of detection graphs & recovery

IDENTIFICATION.evidence: A deadlock occurs when a set of concurrent processes is permanently blocked because each process holds at least one resource and is waiting for another resource.

MEANING.evidence: Four simultaneous conditions—known as the Coffman conditions—must hold: Mutual Exclusion, Hold and Wait, No Preemption, Circular Wait.

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.evidence: Data structures for n processes and m resource types: Available, Max, Allocation, Need matrix where Need[i,j] = Max[i,j] - Allocation[i,j].

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.evidence: Safe sequence <P0, ..., Pn> definition: Work = Available, Work = Work + Allocation[i] when Need[i] <= Work.

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.evidence: Brief mention of ordering F(R) breaking circular wait but degrading utilization; missing deep mathematical justification of three-way trade-offs against detection/recovery.

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.evidence: Full worked numerical trace on 3 processes P0, P1, P2 and 3 resources A, B, C; step-by-step vector subtractions proving unsafe state.

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.evidence: Lecturer explicitly stated: we will not be covering cycle-detection algorithms or checkpoint-rollback recovery strategies in this session due to time.

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.evidence: Distributed deadlock detection and consensus not discussed in lecture.

IDENTIFICATION.diagnosis: Deadlock condition and resource contention formally defined.

MEANING.diagnosis: Four Coffman conditions articulated and explained thoroughly.

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.diagnosis: Banker's Algorithm matrices (Available, Max, Allocation, Need) formalized.

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.diagnosis: Safe sequence invariant and dynamic Work vector updates demonstrated.

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.diagnosis: Three-way trade-offs between prevention, avoidance, and recovery only briefly mentioned without formal proof or comparative analysis.

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.diagnosis: Complete step-by-step numerical execution trace discovering unsafe state.

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.diagnosis: Detection and recovery mechanisms (wait-for graphs, victim rollback) explicitly omitted due to time.

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.diagnosis: Distributed deadlock mechanisms are non-mandatory extension outside today's single-node OS scope.

pkg_08_biochem_kinetics.topic: Michaelis-Menten Enzyme Kinetics and Lineweaver-Burk Analysis

children.name: E + S <-> ES -> E + P Kinetic Model

episodes.dominant_concept: Enzymatic reaction model E + S <-> ES -> E + P
Briggs-Haldane steady-state derivation of v0 equation
Meaning of Vmax and Km affinity index
Lineweaver-Burk double reciprocal plot & inhibition comparison
Scope limitation: Allosteric cooperativity and Hill equation postponed

IDENTIFICATION.evidence: Enzyme, substrate, intermediate enzyme-substrate complex [ES], and product formation defined.

MEANING.evidence: Vmax explained as asymptotic limit where all enzyme active sites are occupied; Km explained as substrate concentration at half-Vmax reflecting affinity.

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.evidence: Rate constants k1, k-1, k2; enzyme balance [E]t = [E] + [ES]; steady state assumption d[ES]/dt = 0.

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.evidence: Biochemical justification: why steady state holds when [S] >> [E] and why initial velocity prevents reverse reaction.

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.evidence: Double reciprocal Lineweaver-Burk equation derived; competitive (same y-intercept, altered x-intercept) vs non-competitive (altered y-intercept, same x-intercept) contrasted.

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.evidence: Lecturer explicitly stated: we will not be discussing allosteric enzymes or non-hyperbolic sigmoidal Hill curves today; those are postponed to next week.

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.evidence: Metabolic pathway flux control and pharmacokinetic applications not taught.

pkg_09_discrete_math_trees.topic: Spanning Trees, Cut Property, and Kruskal's Algorithm with DSU

children.name: Minimum Spanning Tree Total Weight Minimization
Disjoint Set Union (DSU) Find/Union with Path Compression

episodes.dominant_concept: Spanning tree definition and |V|-1 edges
Cut property theorem and exchange argument proof
Kruskal algorithm & DSU data structure
Step-by-step trace on 5-vertex graph
Kruskal vs Prim algorithm comparison
Scope limitation: Disconnected graphs and negative weights omitted

IDENTIFICATION.evidence: Let G = (V, E) be a connected, undirected graph with positive real edge weights. A spanning tree T is an acyclic connected subgraph containing all vertices, with |V|-1 edges.

MEANING.evidence: Minimum Spanning Tree minimizes total edge weight sum w(e).

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.evidence: Cut (S, V\S), crossing edges, DSU Find(u), Union(u,v) with union-by-rank and path compression, O(m log m) complexity.

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.evidence: Cycle prevention: Find(u) == Find(v) detects cycles; Find(u) != Find(v) triggers edge addition and union.

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.evidence: Rigorous cut-and-paste exchange argument proving that strictly minimum crossing edge must belong to every MST by contradiction.

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.evidence: Step-by-step trace on 5 vertices A, B, C, D, E; 7 sorted edges evaluated; edges (B,D) and (A,C) discarded to avoid cycles; total weight = 10.

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.evidence: Lecturer explicitly stated: we are completely skipping disconnected forests, negative edge weights, and directed branchings today due to time constraints.

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.evidence: Euclidean TSP approximation via MST doubling not discussed in lecture.

IDENTIFICATION.diagnosis: Spanning tree and graph primitives formally identified.

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.diagnosis: Cut definitions and DSU data structures formalized.

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.diagnosis: Cut Property theorem proved with rigorous exchange argument.

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.diagnosis: Worked Kruskal trace on 5 nodes executed.

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.diagnosis: Disconnected graphs (spanning forests), negative weights, and directed graphs explicitly skipped.

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.diagnosis: TSP heuristics and Steiner trees are optional extensions.

pkg_10_microecon_game_theory.topic: Strategic Form Games, Dominance Solvability, and Pure Nash Equilibrium

children.name: Players N, Strategy Sets Si, Payoff Functions ui
Strict Dominance Inequality: ui(s'', s_-i) > ui(s', s_-i)
Iterated Elimination of Strictly Dominated Strategies
Mutual Best Responses & No Profitable Unilateral Deviation
Underline Method for Finding Pure Equilibria

episodes.dominant_concept: Primitives of strategic form games and bi-matrix
Strict dominance definition & IESDS elimination
Nash equilibrium & best-response underline method
Prisoner's Dilemma: dominant strategy & Pareto inefficiency
Scope limitation: Coordination games & mixed strategies postponed

IDENTIFICATION.evidence: Strategic form game primitives: finite player set N = {1,...,n}, pure strategy set Si, and payoff function ui: S -> R.

MEANING.evidence: Strict dominance defined with strict inequality for all opponent profiles; Nash equilibrium defined as mutual best responses.

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.evidence: Bi-matrix structure with payoff pairs (u1, u2); IESDS iterative elimination algorithm.

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.evidence: Best-response underline method: row player max underlined per column, column player max per row.

JUSTIFICATION_WHY.evidence: Theoretical proof of Pareto suboptimality: individual rational dominance leads to (1,1) which is strictly inferior to (3,3).

APPLICATION_INTERPRETATION.evidence: Full worked payoff matrix solution of Prisoner's Dilemma showing Defect dominates Cooperate.

BOUNDARIES_EXCEPTIONS.evidence: Lecturer explicitly stated: we will NOT be discussing mixed strategies, expected utility with probabilities, or focal points in coordination games today; postponed to next week.

TRANSFER_SYNTHESIS.evidence: Verbal mention that game theory applies to environmental pollution and arms races, but no formal modeling.

STRUCTURE_COMPONENTS.diagnosis: Bi-matrix representation and IESDS procedure formalized.

RELATIONSHIPS_MECHANISM.diagnosis: Best-response correspondence and underline method demonstrated.
